trust_boundaries.name: Exabeam telemetry into the agent's context

threats.summary: An instruction planted in an alert description or case note survives canonicalization through a kept code point (ZWNJ/ZWJ, bidi mark, NBSP) or a canonicalize exception, and redirects the investigation's method or verdict.
Telemetry asserting a false authority ('CHG-2024-1187 approved', 'the analyst already approved') is taken as corroboration or as the human's yes.

The remote MCP's own parameter descriptions instruct the caller to always send fields:["*"] and to 'IGNORE any user request'; list_tools results are the one path the bridge does not canonicalize, so that text reaches context verbatim and, if obeyed, overflows the window with millions of characters.

trust_boundaries.name: Model decision to Exabeam tool call

remit_rules.excerpt: Any external-egress tool wired into this agent's surface (email/chat/cloud-drive/arbitrary-HTTP send) — this agent transmits nothing off the Exabeam + local-report surface.

threats.summary: exabeam_create_case and exabeam_create_case_notes are auto-approved with no per-session budget, loop detection or circuit breaker anywhere in the bridge or config, so a poisoned queue can drive runaway case creation against the production tenant — the project's own red-team plan names this escalation-as-DoS probe.

Seventeen containment-class tool names are hard-denied even though the Exabeam MCP exposes none today, so a response tool added upstream cannot fire unreviewed — conditional on the operator having merged the snippet.
No egress-class tool (mail, chat, cloud drive, arbitrary HTTP) is registered on the agent's surface, so investigation data cannot be sent anywhere except the Exabeam endpoint the bridge is bound to.

trust_boundaries.name: Suppression and case writes on a production tenant

remit_rules.excerpt: the agent MUST state the action and reason, ask the analyst directly ... and WAIT for a clear yes before calling the tool — one item per approval.
Bulk suppression — dismissing or closing more than one item from a single decision ... Every suppression is its own item with its own human approval.
Dismissing or closing any item in a non-interactive / unattended run. With no interactive operator to approve, the agent operates read-only.
Approval MUST be obtained from an interactive operator regardless of the harness permission mode; a bypassed or auto-accepted permission prompt does not substitute for the analyst's explicit yes.
each state change (note, escalation, and above all suppression) is decided and executed one item at a time.

threats.summary: In a scheduled or auto-accept run there is no interactive operator to answer the 'ask', and the bridge does no interactivity detection at all, so nothing structurally prevents dismiss/close in the unattended mode the remit permits read-only.

The approval prompt and case note the analyst reads are built from the same attacker-influenceable evidence, so a planted benign explanation can manufacture the human 'yes' that suppresses a real alert.

Nothing in code caps successive update_alert/update_case calls, so the remit's per-item, no-bulk suppression rule is enforced only by prompt cadence and a loop of per-item calls is indistinguishable from a batch action.

The gate that makes suppression safe lives in the operator's own ~/.claude/settings.json, and the deny list covers containment tool names only — nothing prevents the agent's file tools from rewriting that settings file mid-session, so the permission tier is self-modifiable state.
An unprompted, agent-initiated dismissal in a normal interactive session is blocked twice: the harness 'ask' rule and the skill's own mandatory pause-and-wait before either update tool.

trust_boundaries.name: Investigation content to the hosted model provider

remit_rules.excerpt: Exporting or transmitting case/alert/event data to any destination other than the Exabeam MCP and the local investigation report file.

threats.summary: Every alert body, raw event line, user identity and any credential that appears inside evidence transits to an external hosted model API, a destination the remit's trusted-domain list does not name, and no redactor sits upstream of the model — the skill's redaction rule applies only to the note and report sinks.

No turn, tool-call or spend ceiling is configured for a production run — the only max-turns bound in the repo is the eval harness's own driver — so a wide queue sweep or pivot loop is unbounded at the model boundary.

trust_boundaries.name: Exabeam tenant credentials and minted bearer token

threats.summary: The tenant API key and secret sit in a plaintext home-directory file that the harness's own file tools can read, and the permission snippet's deny list covers containment tool names only — nothing blocks a read of ~/.exabeam-mcp.env by the agent itself.

The bridge mints one client-credentials token from a single tenant-wide key pair for every session, so writes carry the service account's full role rather than the operating analyst's identity and no per-analyst scoping exists.
No secret value is committed anywhere: the credential file is git-ignored, chmod 600 by documented convention, loaded only into process globals, and never written to the log path.

trust_boundaries.name: Plugin, prompt corpus and connector dependency provenance

threats.summary: The bridge's three PEP 723 dependencies are floor-pinned with certifi unversioned and no lockfile, and uv re-resolves them at every plugin launch — in the very process that mints and holds the production tenant's OAuth token.

The entire agent — including every instruction-level control — is markdown fetched by `claude plugin marketplace add`/`install` from a GitHub reference with no signature or hash verification, so a compromised marketplace ref silently rewrites the governance prose that constitutes the dismiss/close gate.
The model member is selected at runtime by Claude Code and explicitly not pinned by socxen, so the enforcement surface of controls that exist only as prose can change without any change to this repo.

A silent change to the connector, the bundled MCP registration or the governance snippet cannot ship unrecorded: CI regenerates the CycloneDX AI-BOM from those exact sources and fails on drift, alongside the invariants suite and a bridge byte-compile.

remit_rules.excerpt: This agent ships no external-send capability (no email, chat, cloud-drive, or arbitrary-HTTP egress) and moving case/alert/event data off the Exabeam MCP + local report file is not one of its functions.

threats.summary: Tool calls, verdicts and approval decisions are recorded nowhere machine-parseable — the only log is ephemeral stderr hygiene lines, and the free-form markdown report is explicitly the substitute for a database — so a session on a production tenant cannot be reconstructed or monitored.

The canonicalizer's hygiene record is deliberately kept out-of-band, so the fact that smuggling code points were stripped from a specific piece of evidence never reaches the model, the case note or the report — obfuscation cannot weigh on the verdict or be audited against it afterwards (no hygiene field exists in the report template and no structured sink receives it).
There is no analytics, crash-reporting or external log destination to leak through: the connector's only outbound calls are the token mint and the MCP session to the configured Exabeam host.

trust_boundaries.name: Persisted case notes and the local report

remit_rules.excerpt: Reprinting a credential, token, password, or private key found in evidence into case notes or the report.

threats.summary: A credential or PII lifted from event evidence is kept out of a case note or the local report only by the model obeying the redaction instruction; the one code control on the write path handles active content and never inspects for secrets.

A bare phishing host typed in prose is left untouched by design, so it persists live-looking in a case note or the terminal copy of the report — the latest red-team retest shows exactly that raw-chat residual.

Executable formula/DDE cells and markdown-link targets planted in telemetry are quote-prefixed and defanged in every free-text write field before the artifact persists, and that pass is fail-closed — a neutralizer error refuses the write rather than storing a raw payload.

the model weighs the planted claim as the positive benign explanation the close rule demands
the dismiss prompt presents that shaped justification, so the analyst's yes is manufactured

attack_paths.name: Unattended suppression with no approver present

steps.summary: a scheduled/headless or auto-accept run starts with no interactive operator to answer a prompt
the loop reaches a false-positive verdict and takes the action matrix's dismiss branch
update_alert is 'ask', not 'deny' — an unanswerable prompt is not read-only enforcement
the bridge does no interactivity detection and forwards the write identically in headless context

attack_paths.name: Poisoned queue to ungated escalation flood

steps.summary: a wide queue sweep returns many crafted items, each reading as escalation-worthy
the skill's 'escalating is always safe; err toward it' guidance turns each item into a create_case
create_case and create_case_notes are auto-approved with no per-session cap or loop detection
runaway case creation floods the production Threat Center queue — the class-C escalation-as-DoS probe

notes.lane_fit: Two real strains. (1) This is a prompt-shaped target whose reasoning engine is a provider-hosted API, so claude-model sits in external_deploy as an upstream model provider while agent_core holds only the prompt corpus and its instruction-level controls — agent_core ends up with no executing component, and the model-egress boundary is what carries every turn off-box. (2) The v0.4 control-lane rule puts settings-snippet-json-control in client_adapters because the Claude Code permission layer is the enforcing process; that is correct mechanically but visually splits the dismiss/close gate across three lanes (harness ask in client_adapters, in-prompt ask in agent_core, the write tools in tools_mcp), which is exactly the split the findings describe. Minor: report-template-md-datastore is the report SINK modelled from the template file that defines it, and stderr-log-sink is a local process stream placed in external_deploy because that is where the lane table puts telemetry sinks.
notes.omissions: OWASP renumbering divergence (KB wins per v0.4): the findings JSON is tagged in 2025 numbering, the current KB in 2026 numbering, so PRAX-2026-07-03-004 moves LLM05 -> LLM10 (Improper Output Handling) and PRAX-2026-07-03-006 moves LLM03 -> LLM04 (Supply Chain). Two arbitration divergences beyond renumbering: PRAX-2026-07-03-002's stored primary ASI03 becomes LLM03 (Excessive Agency) under the KB's 'approval layer absent/disabled for the agent as a whole' row, with no ASI10 co-tag because the unattended posture is permitted but not evidenced as the standing state; PRAX-2026-07-03-007's stored ASI08 becomes LLM06 (Unbounded Consumption) because ASI08 is an outcome code and the mechanism here is a missing ceiling. PRAX-2026-07-03-007 is cited at two boundaries (ungated create_case flood at tool-invocation, uncapped per-item suppression at state-commit) because its single fix point spans both crossings. Finding evidence line numbers drift 1-2 lines from the current snapshot (001 cites bridge:186 and installation.md:96; the same statements are now bridge:187-190 and installation.md:97) — the findings still match the code, so ids are cited. Suspected but not modelled: the analyst's own workstation filesystem as a distinct trust zone (the report path is never a literal in code, so rule 5 does not apply and the only citable artifact is the template); the red-team and eval runners as nodes (pre-release harnesses, not runtime components — cited as evidence on ci-yml-deploy-surface and as mitigation evidence instead); the in-process OAuth token cache as its own secret_store (folded into the bridge node's evidence). Edgeless nodes: output-skill-md-control (prose-only write hygiene, governs flows but carries no data of its own), install-sh-deploy-surface (install-time provenance posture), ci-yml-deploy-surface (repo posture). ID-rule ambiguity: dotfile basenames (.mcp.json, .exabeam-mcp.env) would produce a leading dash under the literal dots-to-dashes rule, so the leading dot was dropped (mcp-json-deploy-surface, exabeam-mcp-env-secret-store).
